newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. chief welcomes Israel-Palestinian accord.
newsitem.headline: U.N. chief welcomes Israel-Palestinian accord.

text.p: Secretary-General Kofi Annan hailed Wednesday's agreement between Israel and the Palestinians on Hebron and other issues and said he hoped it would lead to further progress in the Middle East peace process.

"The secretary-general is very much encouraged by the conclusion of an agreement regarding Hebron and other important issues which has now been reached between Israel and the Palestinians," a statement issued through a U.N. spokesman said.

"He considers this to be an important achievement, which he hopes will now pave the way for further progress towards the full implementation of the process envisaged in the Declaration of Principles agreed in Oslo," the statement added, referring to a 1993 accord that provided a basis for further negotiations.
Security Council members also welcomed the Hebron agreement but did not issue a formal statement.

After consultations on a number of topics, council President Hisashi Owada of Japan told reporters the United States informed the council of the accord "and the sense of the council was to welcome the fact that the agreement has finally been initialed." But the matter was not discussed in detail, he added.
